transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I’m here because I keep getting stuck checking things. Like, it sounds small when I say it, but I’ll lose hours rechecking my dressing supplies, or the door locks, or dimensions on work files, revision notes… all of that.

I’m an engineer, so checking details is kind of part of the job, and people joke about engineers being picky, but this feels different. I can’t just look once and move on. It’s like I don’t feel allowed to continue until I’ve gone through the same routine enough times that the anxiety finally drops a bit. Then I can move, but by then I’ve wasted so much time.
Do you find that these checking behaviors are accompanied by intrusive, unpleasant thoughts or fears that won’t go away unless you perform the check?

Yeah… yes, that’s pretty much it. Even when I know I’ve cleaned around a wound properly, or I’ve gone through a CAD file and the numbers look right, this thought just cuts back in like, “What if you missed one tiny thing?” And then it’s not just annoying, it feels like it could turn into something serious, like an infection or some design mistake that hurts someone.

I mean, I know logically that I’ve already checked it—like I can literally remember checking it—but it doesn’t settle. I’ll try to tell myself it’s fine, and then my brain sort of loops back to the same “but what if” thing. It’s kind of like when you’re leaving for a trip and you keep thinking you forgot your passport, except… I don’t know, way more intense and with worse consequences in my head.
Do these intrusive thoughts make you feel that something terrible will happen if you don’t check, and does checking help reduce that feeling of dread or anxiety?

Yes… that’s what it feels like. Like if I don’t check, I’m not really allowed to move on because something could be wrong and I’d be the person who missed it.

It happens with a bunch of things—my dressing supplies, the door locks, work files, dimensions, revision notes. I’ll start checking one thing and then it turns into this whole routine. And I know that probably sounds like normal “being careful,” especially in engineering, where everyone is always talking about tolerances and revision control and all that… but I’ll lose hours to it.

The checking does help, kind of. Not because I feel confident, exactly, but because after I’ve gone through it enough times, the anxiety drops enough that I can finally stop. Then later I’m annoyed with myself because I spent so much time on it.
When you’re checking these things, is it strictly to make sure everything is perfect, or is it more about needing to follow a specific routine or set of steps to feel less anxious?

It’s more the routine, I think. Like, I do want it to be right, obviously—especially with work files and dimensions, because that stuff matters—but the part that feels… not normal is that I can’t move on until I’ve checked it in this certain sequence enough times.

Like with dressing supplies or the locks, I’ll tell myself, okay, just check once, but then I’m back doing it again because it doesn’t feel settled. And then I’ll remember some totally unrelated time in college where I forgot one small thing before a lab and it caused this whole delay, and suddenly I’m using that as proof that I need to check again, even though it’s not really connected.

So yeah, it’s not just perfection. It’s that I feel sort of stuck until I’ve gone through the steps and the anxiety drops a bit. Then I can finally move on, but sometimes that’s after I’ve lost hours.
When you’re going through your checking routine, is it more about trying to quiet a feeling of anxiety or discomfort, even if you know the chances of something being wrong are very low?

Yeah, it’s definitely more about quieting that feeling than actually believing there’s a high chance something is wrong.

Like, I can know the door is locked, or the file dimensions are fine, or that I already checked the dressing supplies, but it’s like my brain won’t give me permission to move on yet. I have to go through the same routine again until the anxiety drops enough. And sometimes that means I lose hours just rechecking locks, revision notes, measurements… stuff that should take a few minutes.

It’s frustrating because part of me is aware the risk is probably low, but the discomfort doesn’t match that. It still feels urgent.

Can you describe what happens if you try to resist doing the checking routine? Does it increase your anxiety significantly, and do you feel like you have to complete the routine to avoid something bad happening?

If I try to resist it, I get really tense, yeah. Like I’ll walk away from the door or the file and then I’m still thinking about it, and it’s like I haven’t actually left it behind.

What usually brings me in circles is that I don’t feel allowed to move on until I’ve done the checking routine enough times that the anxiety drops. It happens with the dressing supplies, the locks, file dimensions, revision notes… and I know that sounds like just being careful, but it can take hours.

I’ll tell myself, “Just leave it, you already checked,” and then I’ll get this dread that something is off and I’m choosing to ignore it. So I go back and do the steps again, not even because I’m finding anything new, just because completing it makes the feeling calm down a little.
Besides checking things repeatedly, do you feel you need to perform any other specific behaviors or mental acts in a certain way to reduce anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Mostly it’s the checking. I mean, I do it in a very specific order sometimes, so maybe that counts as “a certain way,” but I’m not, like… doing a separate ritual outside of that, I don’t think.

It’s more that I get stuck rechecking the same things—my dressing supplies, the door locks, dimensions on files, revision notes—until it feels like I’ve done it enough times and the anxiety finally drops. And then suddenly I’ve lost an hour or two. Sometimes more.

It reminds me of when I’m working on a drawing package and you zoom in too far, and then you’re checking tiny details that nobody else would even notice, but you can’t zoom back out. Sorry, that’s probably not the best example. But yeah, the main thing bringing me in is the rechecking.

Are there any other types of intrusive or unwanted thoughts that come into your mind, even if they’re not related to checking, that cause you distress or make you feel like you need to do something to neutralize them?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not always a whole different category, but the thought itself feels intrusive.

Like even after I’ve cleaned a wound area properly, or reviewed a CAD file and I know I looked at it, this thought cuts in like, “What if you missed one tiny thing?” And then my brain jumps to, like, infection, or a design mistake that somehow hurts someone. Which… I know that sounds dramatic, because usually it’s just a small detail or something I already checked.

It’s weird because I can explain to myself that I did the steps, I reviewed it, I cleaned it, whatever—but it doesn’t really land. I can’t just reason it away. It keeps poking at me until I feel like I need to go back and do something about it.
